meta.title: Reconciliation Ledger — Round 2 (post-9f975e4 feature wave)
meta.description: Round-2 ledger of the standing cross-project-sync procedure (engineering/maintenance/cross-project-sync.md). Scope: Xcind PRs #82/#83/#85/#86/#87/#88 (the round-1 known_excluded set) triaged against Scind canon at ca156eb, which round 1 left otherwise unchanged. RL- IDs continue the global sequence from the closed P6 ledger (RL-001..RL-115). Same field names and status vocabulary as the P6 ledger.
inputs: Step-1 gate: LDS self-sync audit ce0da4c (docs-only, scoped to exactly these PRs) + make check green (137/137)

action_types.CANON-CHANGE: Edit existing Scind canon (design proved wrong/incomplete).
action_types.PROMOTE: Add a new capability to Scind canon.
action_types.CANON-CONFIRM: Annotate/verify Scind canon as validated by Xcind (low priority).
action_types.DIVERGENCE: Covered by / recorded against the P7 divergence registry.
action_types.DELIBERATELY-DEFERRED: Deliberate Xcind deviation already admitted to the registry.
action_types.REGISTRY-UPDATE: Status change to an existing P7 registry entry (Step 5 outcome).
action_types.NO-DELTA: Triaged; no canon or registry impact.

rows.title: External proxy mode (managed|external) as canon + new Scind ADR-0017
rows.edit_sketch: New ADR modeled on Xcind ADR-0022: proxy.mode managed|external; external never starts/stops/configures a proxy; apps join a configured shared network with labels retargeted via proxy.network/http_entrypoint/https_entrypoint/certresolver; single label-generation code path; two network topologies with platform-recreation caveat. Credits Xcind PR #83 as validating implementation.
rows.notes: Headline of round 2. Canon already names the externally-managed-proxy case (auto_start:false) but cannot deliver it; gap is three hardcoded values wide.

rows.title: proxy.mode config key, reconciled with proxy.auto_start
rows.edit_sketch: Add proxy.mode to proxy.yaml schema/table. external supersedes auto_start (short-circuits before it is read); network-ensure failure is a hard error in external mode. Reframe the auto_start:false opt-out paragraph against the new mode.

rows.title: Configurable proxy.network (default scind-proxy)
rows.edit_sketch: One config key drives traefik.docker.network label, providers.docker.network, and the compose networks block; default reproduces current behavior byte-for-byte.

rows.title: Configurable entrypoint names (proxy.http_entrypoint/https_entrypoint)
rows.edit_sketch: Entrypoint NAMES become config (defaults web/websecure) driving both generated static config and router labels; ports were already configurable.

rows.title: proxy.certresolver + tls.certresolver router label (first ACME path in canon)
rows.edit_sketch: When proxy.certresolver is set, append tls.certresolver to every HTTPS router (per-export and apex) in BOTH modes; distinguish which-routers-exist (tls.mode) from who-provisions-certs (resolver).

rows.title: External-mode TLS division of labor; tls.mode custom x external = hard error
rows.edit_sketch: External mode skips the whole cert cascade (host proxy terminates TLS); router emission rules unchanged; custom+external MUST be rejected at validation/init.

rows.title: Command-behavior matrix under mode: external (refusal over silent no-op)
rows.edit_sketch: init/up succeed with redefined contracts; up --force, down, restart, logs refuse with exit 1; principle: refusal beats silent no-op for verbs promising actions on a proxy Scind does not own.

rows.title: Two-predicate down escape hatch for managed-to-external migration
rows.edit_sketch: down still stops a leftover managed proxy iff scind.component=proxy container is running AND the generated managed compose file exists; both predicates load-bearing.

rows.title: External init: managed-artifact cleanup + compose-file retention rule
rows.edit_sketch: Remove stale static config + dynamic/tls.yaml; keep certs/; remove compose file ONLY when no managed proxy container is running (else it is the only stopping handle) + warn. Coolify-style example.

rows.title: Network topology guidance (join host proxy's network vs connect ours)
rows.edit_sketch: RECOMMENDED: point proxy.network at the host proxy's existing network (external:true overrides; host proxy container untouched). ALTERNATE: docker network connect, re-applied on every container recreation (platform hosts recreate on upgrade). Absent network still created + loud warning.

rows.title: Known caveats: entrypoint-level redirect shadowing; providers.docker.constraints
rows.edit_sketch: Host Force-HTTPS shadows emitted HTTP routers (harmless); constrained host providers need the constraint label added manually. Converts two silent-mystery support cases into a paragraph.

rows.title: redirectscheme.permanent=true (301, not Traefik's default 302)
rows.edit_sketch: Add the permanent=true label to the shared redirect middleware definition; tls: require is a stable policy, permanent redirect is the correct, cacheable semantic.

rows.title: noop@internal pin + per-service middleware emission already in canon
rows.edit_sketch: Xcind ce0da4c caught its own docs up to canon; Scind already specifies both with Validated-by-Xcind annotations. Only cosmetic table completeness, riding along with RL-127.

rows.title: proxy status + doctor must report mode; network check replaces Traefik check externally
rows.edit_sketch: Mode line in both outputs + external sample; doctor: 'Proxy network: present' is the hard diagnostic under external (overrides declare it external:true), Traefik-running check dropped, detected-container line informational.

rows.title: External-mode teardown must never remove the shared proxy network
rows.edit_sketch: Teardown may stop a retained managed proxy via the old compose file (state kept for retry on failure) and removes generated state, but never the configured shared network (foreign-owned, shared with unrelated workloads).
rows.notes: Merged into the RL-131 proxy destroy spec.

rows.title: scind proxy destroy [--purge] [--force] (canon has no proxy teardown verb)
rows.edit_sketch: Stop proxy, remove generated state incl. the assigned-port inventory (call out: every workspace loses port assignments), config only with --purge; add 'proxy destroyed' as a third port-release trigger in state-management.md. Credits Xcind PR #86.

rows.title: workspace destroy failure semantics (abort before state removal)
rows.edit_sketch: If any app teardown fails, destroy aborts before removing .generated/, workspace.yaml, ports, registry entry; already-stopped apps stay stopped; retry is safe.

rows.title: xcind-application dispose converges with canonical scind app remove
rows.edit_sketch: Functionally equivalent sequence; Xcind implemented what canon specified. No edit.

rows.title: Directory-removal flag shape: --yes/--rm split vs --force/--keep-apps pair
rows.target: xcind: noted in divergence 0034 resolution note (no new registry entry)
rows.edit_sketch: Earned sentence: Scind's --force/--keep-apps already reaches the same two non-interactive outcomes as Xcind's --yes/--rm split, so there is no capability gap to close. Naming-level; beneath registry granularity.
rows.notes: Recorded inside 0034's closure note rather than minting a registry entry.

rows.title: Close divergence 0034: Xcind converged via dispose (PR #86)
rows.edit_sketch: Premise 'Xcind has no destroy verb' is now false: xcind-workspace dispose does the same down+release-ports+remove-generated+deregister cascade as scind workspace destroy. Not a canon change (canon validated); flip Active -> Resolved with convergence note; re-check 0026's destroy-facet wording next round.
rows.notes: Both the dispose triage and the Step 5 re-audit reached the same conclusion independently. Applied 2026-08-07: 0034 entry + registry.json + README flipped to Resolved.

rows.title: scind app get <path>: single-value resolved-config lookup
rows.target: scind: engineering/reference/cli.md (new subsection after app exports + JSON-contract cross-link)
rows.edit_sketch: Adopt the path grammar (dotted segments, quoted keys, [N] indices) and exit-code contract; NOT the --cached/--hooks-ttl cache mechanics (Xcind-cache-specific, see divergence 0020). Credits Xcind PR #85.

rows.title: resolve-specific --help (Xcind PR #87): no canon impact
rows.edit_sketch: Bespoke help text exists only because Xcind hand-rolls arg parsing; a cobra-style CLI generates per-subcommand help without static-text drift risk. Scind should not adopt.

rows.title: PR #88 re-confirms the generation-ordering rule canon already states
rows.target: scind: engineering/specs/workspace-lifecycle.md (Generation Logic step 10, one clause)
rows.edit_sketch: Canon step 10 already mandates live-state-derived resolution before artifact writes, annotated Validated-by-Xcind. PR #88 is a second independent confirmation; append one clause, no new normative content.

rows.title: kislyuk/yq compatibility (PR #82) fully covered by divergence 0001
rows.edit_sketch: Bash-runtime portability concession; Scind's Go stack has no shelled-out yq. Covered by 0001 (Bash vs Go) + 0008 (runtime dep checker). No action.

rows.title: Dashboard is not an entrypoint; fix blanket web-redirect wording
rows.target: scind: engineering/specs/proxy-infrastructure.md (Entry Points table) + reference/configuration.md examples
rows.edit_sketch: Remove the dashboard|8080 entrypoint row (dashboard rides Traefik's insecure-API listener via api block + port publish, no entryPoints block); note dashboard inert under external mode; fix 'redirects to HTTPS' to per-export tls: require only.

rows.title: proxy init flag surface for the five new keys: covered by divergence 0036
rows.edit_sketch: Xcind exposes the keys as init flags because its sourceable-shell config has no structured editor (registry 0036, accepted 2026-08). Scind routes them through scind config set proxy.*; only the schema keys land (RL-117..RL-120).

rows.title: Round-2 artifact refresh: map + ADR table + Step 5 stamps + watermark
rows.edit_sketch: Update 12 materially-changed correspondence rows, add 3 (Xcind ADRs 0021/0022; handoff row if absent), flip the targeting ADR row SCIND-ONLY -> DIVERGED-DECISION (Scind 0011 vs Xcind 0023), stamp 22 re-audited divergences, append the round-2 baseline entry.
